done_when: send_message returns the host's real delivery result or a clear not-confirmed note, and a rate-limited IPC request waits for the next pass instead of being archived, proven by host and runner tests

findings.body: The remaining test gap from previous finding 2 is still open. This runner test supplies only a signed failure response; it never checks successful confirmation or the no-response timeout. The existing stdio cases at apps/core/test/unit/runner/ipc-mcp-stdio.test.ts:867 and :888 check exit status and request contents, not the returned delivery note. Restoring 'Message sent.' in the timeout branch would therefore leave these tests green. Add runner-boundary assertions for confirmed success and unconfirmed timeout. The small-fix exception removes the end-to-end requirement, but these Done-when behaviours still need proof.
findings.title: Not done: runner tests prove confirmed delivery and the not-confirmed timeout note

findings.body: Every host error is prefixed with 'Message not sent', although some errors explicitly mean delivery occurred. Telegram throws after delivering earlier chunks at apps/core/src/channels/telegram/extracted-helpers.ts:113, and channel wiring also throws after a successful provider send when durable settlement fails at apps/core/src/app/bootstrap/channel-wiring.ts:587. These reach this branch as failure responses, producing contradictory delivery reports and potentially encouraging a full resend. Use a neutral failure prefix or preserve the host's partial/uncertain delivery wording.
findings.title: Preserve uncertainty when delivery was partial or already visible

why: Agents are told a message was sent before it is delivered, and overloaded messages are thrown away
